title: Hero section with headline and action
when: The user wants the top section of a page: a big headline, a supporting line, an action button and an image or background.
inputs: the primary action and its target
prompt:
Goal: A hero that states the offer in one headline, shows one primary action and paints fast without layout shift.
Steps:
1. <section aria-labelledby="hero-title"> with the h1, one paragraph of at most 25 words, a primary link styled as a button and an optional quiet secondary link.
2. Size the h1 with clamp(2rem, 5vw + 1rem, 3.75rem); cap lines near 20ch for the h1 and 60ch for the paragraph.
3. One column on phones; from about 860 px a two column grid with align-items: center.
4. The image gets width, height, alt and fetchpriority="high", never loading="lazy" above the fold; add srcset when sizes exist.
5. Text over a photo gets a dark gradient overlay and a solid background-color fallback to keep 4.5 to 1 contrast.
6. Keep vertical padding moderate so the button shows on a 375 by 667 screen.
Quality bar:
- The headline names the result for the visitor, not a slogan.
- The button reads as a verb plus an object.
- The section still looks finished if the image fails.
Pitfalls:
- Lazy loading the hero image, which delays the largest paint.
- Autoplaying background video with no pause control.
- Two equally loud buttons.
Verify:
- [ ] Exactly one h1, inside the hero.
- [ ] The image has alt, width and height.
- [ ] The button is visible without scrolling at 375 px.
- [ ] Text over images keeps 4.5 to 1.
Output: The hero markup at the top of main and its rules in style.css.

examples.input: hero section for my yoga studio
examples.output: h1 "Calm, strong mornings in Pinheiros", one line, Book a class button, photo with width and height on the right
